questions.question: You need to return only the failed blob requests from the StorageBlobLogs table. Which KQL operator should you use after the table name?

options.text: where StatusCode >= 400
options.why: Correct. The where operator filters rows that match a condition.

options.text: project StatusCode >= 400
options.why: The project operator selects or computes columns. It does not filter rows.

options.text: summarize StatusCode >= 400
options.why: The summarize operator aggregates rows into groups.

options.text: render StatusCode >= 400
options.why: The render operator draws a chart of the results.

questions.explanation: A KQL query starts with a table and pipes rows through operators. where keeps only the rows that satisfy the predicate.

questions.question: You need to display the number of failed requests in 15-minute intervals as a line chart. Which query should you run?

options.text: StorageBlobLogs | where StatusCode >= 400 | summarize count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 15m) | render timechart
options.why: Correct. bin groups the timestamps into 15-minute buckets, summarize counts each bucket and render timechart draws the chart.

options.text: StorageBlobLogs | where StatusCode >= 400 | where TimeGenerated > ago(15m) | render timechart
options.why: ago(15m) limits the rows to the last 15 minutes. It does not create 15-minute intervals.

options.text: StorageBlobLogs | summarize count() by StatusCode | render piechart
options.why: This query counts by status code and draws a pie chart, not a time series.

options.text: StorageBlobLogs | project TimeGenerated, StatusCode | take 15
options.why: take returns 15 rows. It does not aggregate the data into intervals.

questions.explanation: Use summarize with bin(TimeGenerated, interval) for time series and render timechart to draw them.

questions.question: You must identify the users who deleted Azure resources during the last seven days. The activity log is exported to a Log Analytics workspace. Which table should you query?

options.text: AzureActivity
options.why: Correct. Activity log events exported by a subscription diagnostic setting are stored in the AzureActivity table.

options.text: Heartbeat
options.why: The Heartbeat table records agent heartbeats from monitored machines.

options.text: Perf
options.why: The Perf table stores performance counters collected by the Azure Monitor Agent.

options.text: StorageBlobLogs
options.why: StorageBlobLogs contains data-plane requests to Blob Storage.

questions.explanation: Filter AzureActivity on OperationNameValue and ActivityStatusValue and project the Caller column to see who performed delete operations.

questions.question: You run the following query: Heartbeat | summarize LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer | where LastSeen < ago(15m). What does the query return?

options.text: One row for each computer whose most recent heartbeat is older than 15 minutes
options.why: Correct. The query finds the latest heartbeat per computer and keeps only computers that have not reported for 15 minutes.

options.text: All heartbeat records from the last 15 minutes
options.why: The summarize operator reduces the results to one row per computer before the filter is applied.

options.text: The number of heartbeats received in each 15-minute interval
options.why: The query does not use bin and does not count records.

options.text: Computers that sent a heartbeat during the last 15 minutes
options.why: The filter keeps computers whose last heartbeat is earlier than 15 minutes ago.

questions.explanation: This pattern is commonly saved as a log search alert to detect machines that stop reporting.

questions.question: You write a KQL query that returns the top failing callers of a storage account. You need to be notified when the query returns results, and the query must run every 10 minutes. What should you create?

options.text: A log search alert rule that runs the query every 10 minutes and uses an action group
options.why: Correct. Log search alert rules run a KQL query on a schedule and call action groups when the condition is met.

options.text: A metric alert rule on the Transactions metric
options.why: A metric alert evaluates a metric value. It cannot run the KQL query.

options.text: An alert processing rule with a recurring schedule
options.why: Alert processing rules modify alerts that have already fired. They do not run queries.

options.text: A saved query pinned to a dashboard
options.why: A pinned query displays results but does not notify anyone.

questions.explanation: In the Logs toolbar, New alert rule creates a log search alert from the current query.
